title: Egress DNS shadowing & tenant isolation audit following production divergence
creator: Asha Patel
body:
Summary:
Customer (Acme AI) reported intermittent cross-tenant DNS/egress resolution where requests from Tenant-B briefly resolved to Tenant-A private IPs (multi-tenant Dedicated clusters). Impact: 2 customer tenants experienced data-plane leakage for ~8 minutes during a scale event; no plaintext data exfiltration confirmed but serious isolation violation risk.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2026-03-12 09:03: Customer alert (support ticket #SUP-8672) and PagerDuty.
- 09:07: SRE triage — observed DNS responses for private hosted zones returning wrong VPC CIDR for small percentage of requests.
- 09:12: Engineering engaged; reproduced locally in staging with traffic replay.
- 09:30: Temporary mitigation (apply per-tenant egress ACL) deployed to affected nodes; customer traffic isolated.
- 10:45: Full mitigation rollout to cluster finished.

Initial Triage Notes:
- Problem surfaced during autoscaler scale-out (burst allocate of dedicated accelerator pools).
- We observed overlapping SNAT translations and stale conntrack mappings on newly allocated NAT nodes causing responses to be forwarded to the wrong tenant's eni due to ephemeral IP reuse.
- Additional symptom: Route reconciliation job ran concurrently and temporarily attached a host-route that overlapped an existing tenant-specific route during rapid node churn.
- Private DNS (Route53 private hosted zones) showed rapid record propagation and conditional forwarding rules that briefly selected the wrong resolver for some subnet combinations.

Root Cause (multi-factor):
1) Autoscaler race: when launching burst nodes we used shared subnet + shared NAT pools which allowed ephemeral IP reuse before old conntrack entries had expired.
2) Conntrack inertia: conntrack entries on NAT nodes were not flushed when an eni was reassigned, leading to packets being forwarded using stale 5-tuple maps.
3) Route reconciliation: the reconcile loop that writes per-tenant host-routes could, under high concurrency, create transient host-route overlaps due to non-atomic updates across route tables.
4) DNS forwarding precedence: in some dedicated topologies resolver selection favored a resolver attached to the wrong VPC for a handful of subnets during route convergence, causing incorrect private zone answers.

Workaround Applied:
- Immediately pinned affected tenant subnets to dedicated NAT instances (removed sharing) to stop ephemeral IP reuse.
- Added a conntrack prune hook on ENI detach to aggressively remove stale mappings.
- Temporarily slowed autoscaler rapid-burst behavior for impacted customers.

Fix Implemented (PRs & deploy plan):
- Network-runtime change: Add per-tenant ephemeral SNAT pools + enforce ENI-scoped conntrack flush on detach (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7851).
- Route reconciler: Introduced compare-and-swap semantics and per-tenant staging tables to avoid transient overlaps (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cluster-ops/pull/402).
- DNS resolver ordering: Update resolver selection to prefer VPC-attached endpoints based on stable tags and add a short-ttl fallback for private zones during reconciliation (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dns/pull/119).
- Canary rollout: small canary in us-west-2 on dedicated cluster group alpha-2, then progressively widen across Dedicated fleets with automated rollback on connectivity regression.

Validation & Tests:
- Added e2e test harness that replays high-churn autoscaler events with synthetic tenants verifying isolation invariants (tests added: tests/network/isolation_churn_test.py).
- Added unit tests for route reconciler CAS logic and a simulated conntrack cleanup harness.
- Production monitoring: new SLI/alert for cross-tenant ARP/DNS hits and anomalous conntrack reuse rate.

Customer Communication:
- Drafted incident summary and mitigation timeline sent to Acme AI (support ticket update).
- Scheduled follow-up technical review with Acme networking team 2026-03-16.

Postmortem Actions (owners & ETA):
- ENG: Migrate dedicated customers to per-tenant SNAT pools by default (owner: Diego Morales, ETA: 2026-04-10).
- SRE: Add ENI detach conntrack flush library and deploy across NAT fleet (owner: Lena Zhang, ETA: 2026-03-22).
- Infra: Harden route reconcile to be idempotent and add metrics for reconcile latency (owner: Marco Silva, ETA: 2026-03-28).
- Product: Review Dedicated onboarding doc to avoid shared NAT for high-isolation customers (owner: Priya Nair, ETA: 2026-04-02).

Open Questions / Trade-offs:
- Per-tenant SNAT increases IP footprint and NAT node count (cost vs. isolation). We prioritized isolation for affected customers; need pricing/packaging conversation for opt-in vs. default.
- TTL tuning for private DNS during reconcile reduces cache efficiency; we chose short TTL only during reconciliation windows.

Reviewer Feedback & Notes from Code Review:
- Security review (requested) — ensure no plaintext logs include tenant IP mappings (Lance Chen).
- SRE sign-off pending on drain script idempotency (Lena Zhang) — added retries and safe-guard.

Follow-ups (links):
- Runbook update: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/dedicated-network-isolation
- Postmortem doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/postmortems/ENG-31107
- Customer communication draft: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/Support/ENG-31107

Status & Next Steps:
- Code merged to staging and is in review for production canary (PRs linked above).
- Security review scheduled 2026-03-15.
- Plan to close ticket after 1-week canary with no regression and postmortem published.

Notes for on-call engineers:
- If you see cross-tenant DNS/ARP hits: trigger immediate mitigation script (scripts/isolate_tenant_nat.sh) and escalate to ENG-31107; do not perform ENI reassign without running conntrack prune.

Tags: network, dedicated, isolation, urgent

Attachments: support logs, packet captures and conntrack dumps archived at: s3://redwood-incident-archives/ENG-31107/
